agent_review.notes: All five criteria met on a live codex turn. The pane's longest line is 119 chars (its wrap width) while the extracted reply's longest line is 241 — the authored line, unbroken — so the answer demonstrably came from the rollout JSONL rather than the screen. (1) Both paragraph breaks survive as blank lines. (2) Three list items, each on its own line with its '- ' marker. (3) No break inside any sentence. (4) Directly renderable markdown. (5) Wording, the FMT_ token and punctuation unchanged. Note this is a REGRESSION guard rather than proof of a new fix: codex already preferred its rollout before this certification existed (readCodexTranscriptFinalAssistantText, scoped to promptSentAt). It needs no reconciliation checksum because rollout rows carry wall-clock timestamps, which scope the read to this turn unambiguously — the certainty cursor lacks. This test fails if anyone reverts to pane-derived text or the rollout stops being found.
